Guidelines

content.description: This diagram illustrates instructions for handling tax forms, featuring three main columns with icons. The left column shows a book with check and X marks, a document marked with a green check versus a red X, and restricted symbols like dollar signs. The center column displays a printer icon, a download arrow, and a document icon. The right column includes an envelope with an @ symbol, a printer with a red X, and a graphic of a 2015 NCDOR D-400 tax return form marked with a red X.

content.text: Do not use red ink. Use blue or black ink.

content.description: A graphic titled "Printing" features a central icon of a printer above instructions to set page scaling, flanked by circular panels providing guidelines on ink color usage and submission protocols for document copies.

content.text: Do not use dollar signs, commas, or other punction marks.

content.description: A portion of an instructional infographic featuring a central "Printing" section with a printer icon. To the left, a "Guidelines" section shows a document icon with a red X, and to the right, a "Before" section shows an email icon, advising against using red ink or submitting photocopies.

content.text: Printing

content.description: This infographic features three sections with circular icons representing specific document preparation instructions. The central section focuses on "Printing," illustrated with a printer icon, while the surrounding sections display text and symbols related to guidelines, ink color, and submission requirements for documents.

content.text: Set page scaling to “none.” The Auto-Rotate and Center checkbox should be unchecked.

content.description: A diagram detailing document submission instructions, featuring a central "Printing" section with a printer icon, flanked by panels covering guidelines on ink usage and photocopying requirements.

content.text: Do not select “print on both sides of paper.”

content.description: This infographic segment features a central circle labeled "Printing" with a printer icon, positioned below a partial diagram and flanked by text-heavy columns about submission guidelines and requirements. The layout uses color-coded circular motifs—green for general guidelines and blue for submission instructions—with accompanying icons like a document with a cross, a printer, and an envelope.

content.text: Before You Send

content.description: A diagram features a central "Printing" section with a printer icon, surrounded by instruction circles, including one labeled "elines" with a red ink prohibition symbol and another labeled "Befor Se" featuring an email envelope icon.

content.text: Do not submit photocopies of returns. Submit originals only.

content.description: This infographic features three sections: "Guidelines" on the left, "Printing" in the center, and a "Before Sending" section on the right, each accompanied by relevant icons like a checklist, a printer, and an envelope. The central section instructs users to set page scaling for printing, while the surrounding panels provide formatting and submission instructions, such as using black ink instead of red and submitting original documents rather than photocopies.

content.text: Do not mix form types

content.description: This infographic uses circular icons and color-coded panels to present instructions for document preparation and printing. The central focus is on "Printing," illustrated with a printer icon, while surrounding panels provide guidelines on document formatting, such as avoiding red ink and not using photocopies.

content.text: NC K-1 Supplemental Schedule 2025 Owner or Beneficiary's Share of N.C. Additions and Deductions
DOR Use Only

**A pass-through entity, estate, or trust that reported N.C. additions or N.C. deductions to an owner or beneficiary on a NC K-1 form must provide each owner or beneficiary the information necessary for the owner or beneficiary to prepare the appropriate N.C. tax return. The pass-through entity, estate, or trust may use this schedule to provide the necessary information to the owner or beneficiary. (For more information, see the instructions for the appropriate N.C. tax return.)**
